# Awesome TLS (burp-awesome-tls-plus)

> Burp Suite extension for spoofing browser TLS fingerprints (JA3/JA4/ClientHello) to reduce WAF bot detection. Fork of sleeyax/burp-awesome-tls with per-domain rules and full-tool coverage.

## Project

- Name: Awesome TLS (this fork: burp-awesome-tls-plus)
- Repository: https://github.com/Robin528919/burp-awesome-tls-plus
- Upstream: https://github.com/sleeyax/burp-awesome-tls
- License: GPL-3.0
- Languages: Java (Burp extension UI + HTTP handler), Go (local TLS spoof server via JNA / c-shared)
- Platforms: macOS (x64/arm64), Linux (x86/x64/arm/arm64), Windows (x86/x64)
- Burp: Professional and Community

## One-sentence definition

Awesome TLS hijacks Burp’s outbound HTTP/TLS path and re-sends requests through a local Go server built on utls/tls-client, so destinations observe a chosen browser TLS fingerprint instead of Java’s default stack.

## Who it is for

- Penetration testers and security researchers using Burp Suite
- Users blocked by Cloudflare, Akamai, DataDome, PerimeterX, or similar WAF TLS fingerprinting
- Teams needing different fingerprints per target domain

## What this fork adds (vs upstream)

- Per-domain fingerprint rules (exact host or `*.suffix`), global defaults as fallback
- Spoofing for Proxy, Repeater, Intruder, and Scanner (not Proxy-only)
- Rules stored as shareable JSON outside the Burp project; auto-save; import/export
- Hand-written Swing UI with Burp theme support; several upstream save/forward bugs fixed

## Key capabilities

- Named browser fingerprint profiles (from tls-client / utls mappings)
- Custom ClientHello via hex stream (e.g. from Wireshark)
- Optional intercept proxy to capture and replay a real client fingerprint (global)
- External proxy and timeout overrides per domain rule
- Preserves original HTTP header order when forwarding

## Architecture (short)

1. Burp `HttpHandler` rewrites each eligible request: attaches config in magic header `Awesometlsconfig`, redirects service to local spoof server.
2. Local HTTPS Go server parses config, strips header, builds utls/tls-client with selected fingerprint, forwards to real destination.
3. Response streams back to Burp. Re-entry is avoided by detecting the magic header; Burp suite-internal traffic is skipped.

## Important constraints

- Fingerprint and Hex ClientHello must be overridden as a pair (hex wins if both set).
- Advanced intercept fingerprint is global mutable state — cannot vary per domain.
- New tls-client instance per request (no connection pool across requests).
- Use only on authorized targets; not a complete bot-bypass for JS challenges or IP reputation.
